Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}.$ Differentiating $y(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)$ and applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})})^{′}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}{x}^{′}(t) \\  & =(-A){e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}{x}^{′}(t) \\  & =-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}{x}^{′}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $\text{L2}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by $\text{differentiating and using the product rule}.$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L4}$, $\text{L5}$, and $\text{L6}.$ From $\text{L4}$ we have

$$
y(t)-y({t}_{0})={\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s.
$$

Using $y({t}_{0})=x({t}_{0})$ from $\text{L5}$, this becomes

$$
y(t)-x({t}_{0})={\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s,
$$

so

$$
y(t)=x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s.
$$

Thus, $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L4}$ by substituting $y({t}_{0})=x({t}_{0}).$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ Multiplying both sides of

$$
y(t)=x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,ds
$$

from $\text{L6}$ by ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t) & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L7}$ follows from $\text{L6}$ by $\text{multiplying both sides by }{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}.$

Let's justify each of the selected steps.

  • We first consider lines L1 and L2. Differentiating y(t)=e−A(t−t0)x(t) and applying the product rule gives
    y′(t)=(e−A(t−t0))′x(t)+e−A(t−t0)x′(t)=(−A)e−A(t−t0)x(t)+e−A(t−t0)x′(t)=−Ae−A(t−t0)x(t)+e−A(t−t0)x′(t). Thus, L2 follows from L1 by differentiating and using the product rule.

  • Next, we consider lines L4, L5, and L6. From L4 we have y(t)−y(t0)=∫t0te−A(s−t0)g(s)ds. Using y(t0)=x(t0) from L5, this becomes
    y(t)−x(t0)=∫t0te−A(s−t0)g(s)ds, so y(t)=x(t0)+∫t0te−A(s−t0)g(s)ds. Thus, L6 follows from L4 by substituting y(t0)=x(t0).

  • Finally, we consider lines L6 and L7. Multiplying both sides of y(t)=x(t0)+∫t0te−A(s−t0)g(s)ds from L6 by eA(t−t0) gives
    eA(t−t0)y(t)=eA(t−t0)x(t0)+eA(t−t0)∫t0te−A(s−t0)g(s)ds=eA(t−t0)x(t0)+∫t0teA(t−s)g(s)ds. Therefore, L7 follows from L6 by multiplying both sides by eA(t−t0).
